selected.title: Central concentration across wavelengths
selected.explanation: On identical valid native pixels, the core/surround mean ratio changes from 9.17 to 4.85. Shared block structure remains correlated (0.938); the visual difference survives all nine common contrast settings. These are wavelength-dependent image differences with no assigned physical cause.
limitations: Exploratory numerical summaries; calibration provenance remains UNVERIFIED and scientific measurement suitability is not established.
Shared native mosaic grid and WCS, not independently certified astrometry; no PSF matching or effective-bandpass correction.
No variance extension; neighbor-difference MAD is a descriptive noise proxy, not uncertainty or significance. Correlated noise and unresolved structure can affect it.
Common masks remove missing/rejected pixels, but holes remain visible and the retained sample is not a complete aperture. SOURCE flag is retained; other source-level flags were not propagated.
Core and surrounding annulus are analyst geometry, not validated photometry or blank sky; ratios are not physical flux ratios.

Common display transforms are tested; normalized block structure is a separate diagnostic and is never used to rescale the viewer. No specific physical process, discovery or temporal change is inferred.

geometry.origin: zero-based native FITS lower origin; y=0 at bottom
geometry.block: 4x4 native blocks anchored at (85,85), at least 12/16 common valid pixels, inside radius<=45

method: All 5151 channel pairs. Exact intersection of original visualization masks plus finite IMAGE, NHITS>0, no OVERFLOW/OUTLIER/unknown bits. Reject thresholds in script. Rank coverage*(normalizedStructureMAE+absolute log core/surround ratio change)*minimum display MAE. Greedy diversity: every endpoint must be at least 10 channels from each previously selected endpoint. Isolated annular-level jumps >1.4 relative to median of up to four adjacent channels are excluded as artifact-risk candidates. No per-channel display autoscaling.
